# Summary

This excerpt discusses advances in X-ray microanalysis for layered structures, focusing on the φ(ρz) approach for quantitative analysis. Key points include:

**φ(ρz) Models**: The paper compares two Pouchou and Pichoir models—PAP (parabolic) and XPP (exponential)—describing depth distribution of primary ionization. The XPP model offers "increased flexibility for curve fitting and is mathematically more tractable" and was "found to give the least total error where K and L lines were included in the analysis."

**L-Series Absorption**: For thin films, unresolved L-series lines create significant errors due to absorption coefficient variations. A "weighted average mass absorption coefficient" formula is proposed to improve accuracy by accounting for L₁, L₂, L₃ fluorescence yields and Coster-Kronig transition probabilities.

**Accuracy Claims**: The φ(ρz) method is claimed to achieve "±1 nm" precision in multilayer analysis and depth resolution "comparable to that of Auger sputter profiling."

**Case Study**: Analysis of Ti-BN bilayers (10-15 nm) on silicon demonstrates the method's application to thin film quantification using iterative XPP (EDS) and PAP (WDS) calculations.
